title: How to create a custom view in Linear on Mac: sidebar and filter steps
metaTitle: How to Create a Custom View in Linear on Mac | Step by Step
description: Learn how to create a custom view in Linear on Mac from the sidebar or with ⌥V on a filtered list. Covers sharing rules, editing, and common mistakes.
targetKeyword: how to create a custom view in linear on mac
intro: To create a custom view in Linear on Mac, open Views in the sidebar, choose Issue, Project, or Initiative, and click New view. Or filter a team's list or board, then press ⌥V or click the Save view icon to keep that exact view.
tldr: Sidebar route: open Views, pick Issue, Project, or Initiative, then click New view.
Filter route: add at least one filter to a team's list or board, then press ⌥V.
Team views sit under Issues, Projects, and Initiatives, not in the Views menu.
After saving, Edit view, Duplicate view, and Copy view URL handle changes.

blocks.text: A custom view is a saved version of a list or board in Linear. You set the filters once, save the view, and open it from the sidebar whenever you need it. That helps if you check the same slice of work every day, like open bugs for one team or projects close to a deadline. This guide covers the two ways to make a view on a Mac, where the view ends up, and how to change it later. The steps come from Linear's own help pages. Where those pages say nothing, this guide says so too.
Before you start

items: The Linear desktop app for Mac, or the web app in a current browser.
A workspace where you can create views. Workspace views are available to full members.
An Enterprise plan, if you want a saved initiative view.
At least one filter, if you plan to save from a team's list or board.
An Apple silicon or Intel Mac. Linear's desktop app supports both.

blocks.text: Choose the app first. The desktop app and the web app share almost every feature. Linear's docs say nearly all desktop functionality, including offline mode, is in the web app too. The desktop app still has three advantages on a Mac. It shows OS notifications and unread alerts in the Dock. It has fewer shortcut clashes with browser shortcuts. It also gives you tabs inside the app. This guide uses the desktop app, and it flags where the web app behaves differently.
Create a view from the sidebar

Use this route when you want a view from scratch. Click Views in the left sidebar. Choose a type: Issue, Project, or Initiative. Then click New view. Linear opens a window where you set up the view. The docs do not name every field in that window, so read the labels on screen. Pick the type first, because it decides what the view lists.
Save a filtered list or board with ⌥V

This route is faster when you already see the work you want. Open a team's issue list or board. Add at least one filter. A Save view icon then appears next to the Display Options icon. Click it, or press Option V (⌥V). The filters you chose become a custom view. The shortcut only works when no text box has focus. Click empty space first if the key seems to do nothing.
Team views and the + Create new view button

Linear also lets you attach a view to a team. On a team's issues page, look next to All Issues, Active, and Backlog. You will see a + Create new view button. A view made this way belongs to that team. It appears under Issues, Projects, and Initiatives, not in the Views menu. That is the most common reason people think their view disappeared. Check those three sections before you build a second copy.
Workspace, team, and multi-team scope
Scope decides who sees a view by default, and each scope puts the view in a different place. Choose the scope on purpose. It is easy to share too widely or too narrowly.

items: Workspace view. Appears under Workspace views. Available to full members.
Team view. Appears under Team views in the team, project, or initiative you select.
Multi-team view. Create an All teams view, then refine it with filters.

blocks.text: Edit, duplicate, and copy the link

Changes come after you save. Open the view and click the view name inside it. Choose Edit view to change the name or filters. Choose Duplicate view to make a copy first. That is the safer choice when you want to test a new filter without losing the old one.

items: Rename or change filters: click the view name, then Edit view.
Keep the original: Duplicate view, then edit the copy.
Share a link: open the three-dot menu, then Copy view URL.

blocks.text: Who can see the view and who owns it

The owner defaults to the person who created the view. You can change the owner later. A shared link does not grant access by itself, so share the view first, then send the link. If a teammate can't open a link, check the sharing setting before you blame the link. Workspace views need full member access, so check a person's role if they can't see one.
Display options and the Set as default button

Display options control how a list or board looks. You open them with Shift V (⇧V). The command menu, which opens with ⌘K, also has a Show display options entry. Be careful with one button. Set as default saves the current display options as the default for other workspace members. That changes what your teammates see. Reset to default reverts to the default saved options, so use it after you test a layout.
Worked example: a triage view for one team

Say you run bug triage for a mobile team. You want every open bug that has no owner, so you can assign them in the morning. Start with the team's issues list. Add a filter for the team, one for the bug label, and one for an empty assignee. Your workspace may use different label names, so swap in yours. Press ⌥V and save the view as Mobile triage. The view now sits under Issues for that team. Each morning, one click brings back the same list.
Name the view so you can find it later

Names matter more than they seem. Use the team name and the purpose, such as Mobile triage or Bugs without owner. A name like View 2 hides the purpose within a week. Good names also help teammates who search the Views sections for a list they need.
Check that the view worked

After saving, open the view from the place Linear put it. Confirm the items match the list you filtered from. Then close the view, reopen it from the sidebar, and check again. If the items differ, a filter probably did not save the way you expected. Open Edit view and compare the filters one by one.
Mistakes that waste time
These five slips come up often enough to list here. Each one takes a minute to fix once you spot it.

items: Looking for a team view in the Views menu. Team views live under Issues, Projects, and Initiatives.
Pressing ⌥V on an unfiltered list. The Save view icon only appears after one filter is added.
Typing ⌥V in a search box. The shortcut may do nothing while the text box has focus.
Sending a link before sharing the view. A link alone does not grant access.
Pressing Set as default by accident. Other workspace members get your display options.

blocks.text: Desktop app versus web app on a Mac

The Linear Mac app supports Apple silicon and Intel. It updates itself in the background. If your company manages Macs, you can turn auto-update off with a Terminal command or an MDM plist. Linear's docs give the details for both. The web app runs in the three most recent versions of Chrome, Firefox, and Safari. Shortcuts like ⌥V and ⇧V are more likely to clash with browser shortcuts there, so test them first.
Limits, plans, and old preview notes

Saved initiative views need the Enterprise plan. The docs list no other plan limit for custom views. Linear announced the Views preview on October 27, 2020. Admins turned it on through the command menu, and Option V saved the current list or board as a view. Current docs do not describe a preview. The feature probably went fully live, but no changelog entry confirms it. Linear's docs also give no minimum macOS version, so check the download page before a company-wide rollout.
Next steps after your first view

Once the view works, check its filters against real work for a week. Adjust anything that catches too much or too little. If you want the same items as a board, read [how to switch between list and board in Linear on Mac](/how-to/switch-between-list-and-board-in-linear). For more on filter types, see [how to filter issues in Linear on Mac](/how-to/filter-issues-in-linear). To find commands fast, read [how to open the command menu in Linear on Mac](/how-to/open-the-command-menu-in-linear).

faq.question: Can I create a custom view in the Linear web app on Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. Nearly all desktop features, including offline mode, work in the web app in most browsers. Linear supports the three most recent versions of Chrome, Firefox, and Safari. Browser shortcuts can clash with ⌥V, so test the shortcut in the browser first.

faq.question: Why can't I find my team view in the Views menu?
faq.answer: Team-attached views appear under Issues, Projects, and Initiatives instead. Check those sections before you build a new view, so you do not end up with two copies of the same list.

faq.question: Who owns a custom view?
faq.answer: The creator is the owner by default, and you can change the owner later. Workspace views are available to full members. A shared link does not work until the view itself is shared.

faq.question: Can I make an initiative view on any plan?
faq.answer: No. Saved initiative views are available on the Enterprise plan. The docs list no other plan limit for custom views.

faq.question: How do I change a view after I save it?
faq.answer: Open the view, click the view name inside it, and choose Edit view. To keep the original and test changes, choose Duplicate view first.

faq.question: Does the Linear Mac menu bar list these steps?
faq.answer: Not in the help pages. The official docs describe the sidebar, the on-screen buttons, and keyboard shortcuts. Check the menus in your own version if you want to confirm where each item sits.

task: Create a custom view in Linear on Mac
appliesTo: Linear desktop app for macOS on Apple silicon and Intel Macs
requirements: The Linear desktop app for macOS, or the web app in a current browser
A workspace where you can create views
A full member role for workspace views
At least one filter if you save from a team list or board
An Enterprise plan for saved initiative views

steps.name: Open Linear on your Mac
steps.text: Open the Linear desktop app. Linear's download page lists Mac builds for Apple silicon and Intel. If you use the web app instead, the steps are the same, but browser shortcuts can clash with ⌥V.

steps.name: Click Views in the sidebar
steps.text: Click Views in the left sidebar. The sidebar is the starting point for a view you build from scratch.

steps.name: Choose a view type
steps.text: Pick Issue, Project, or Initiative. Choose the type that matches the items you want to see. Saved initiative views need the Enterprise plan.
steps.tip: If you only need one team's bugs, an Issue view is the usual pick.

steps.name: Click New view
steps.text: Click New view. Linear opens the window where you set up the new view. Keep it open while you finish the setup.

steps.name: Set the name and filters
steps.text: Name the view and add the filters you want. Linear's help pages do not name every field in this window, so read the labels on screen before you continue.
steps.tip: Use a name your teammates will recognize, such as Mobile triage.

steps.name: Or save a filtered list with ⌥V
steps.text: Open a team's issues list or board and add at least one filter. The Save view icon appears next to Display Options. Click it, or press Option V (⌥V), to save the current view.
steps.tip: If the key does nothing, click empty space so no text box has focus.

steps.name: Find the view where Linear put it
steps.text: Team views appear under Issues, Projects, and Initiatives, not in the Views menu. Workspace views appear under Workspace views. Open the section that matches the scope you chose.

shortcuts.action: Save the current filtered list or board as a view

troubleshooting.problem: The Save view icon is missing
troubleshooting.fix: Add at least one filter to a team's list or board. The icon appears next to Display Options only after that.
Click empty space so no text box has focus, then press Option V. You can also click the Save view icon instead.

troubleshooting.problem: I can't find my team view
troubleshooting.fix: Look under Issues, Projects, or Initiatives. Team views do not appear in the Views menu.

troubleshooting.problem: A teammate can't open the shared link
troubleshooting.fix: Share the view first. A link alone does not grant access to the view.

troubleshooting.problem: I can't save an initiative view
troubleshooting.fix: Saved initiative views are available on the Enterprise plan. Check your plan before you troubleshoot further.

troubleshooting.problem: My display change shows up for everyone
troubleshooting.fix: Set as default saves the current display options for other workspace members. Use Reset to default to revert the default.
